issues.text: О22 says the database client library is imported only by «the files of app/server/db/ that ARCH §2.2 names»; ARCH §2.2 names no file of app/server/db, so the block reads it by the layout of ARCH §2: `pg` only in app/server/db/pg.js and @electric-sql/pglite only in app/server/db/pglite.js (the other db files use these adapters). If the design needs `pg` in another db file (for example migrate.js), that is a micro-amendment of criterion 3.

To make the module rule exact, criterion 3 now also reads `require("<m>")` (as written through `createRequire`) as an import, so a banned module cannot come in that way (planted twin red); `node:module` itself stays allowed. The bare core names (`https`, `net`, …) are red through the closed package list.

О24 check in criterion 8: the statement log is the test's own recording of the texts its database adapter sends; the server log of Postgres is not used, because with statement logging switched on Postgres prints bound parameters in its own log (a setting of the host, not measured here).
Not measured: a working server-side form of setting the password on real Postgres and on PGlite (the design shows it, decisions/0116 О24).
